# Bool

`import "std/types"` (included in `import "std"`) · namespace `std.types`

`Bool` parses the usual ways of writing a truth value and converts bools, as
methods of any bool.

```grav
import "std"

fn main() {
    print("${Bool.parse("yes")} ${Bool.parse("OFF")} ${Bool.tryParse("maybe") == null}")
    print("${true.toInt()} ${false.toYesNo()} ${true.toOnOff()} ${"1" as bool}")
}
```

Output:

```text
true false true
1 no on true
```

### class Bool

Truth values (see the top of this file).

**Static members**

- `static fn parse(s: string) -> bool` — "true"/"false", "t"/"f", "yes"/"no", "y"/"n", "on"/"off", "1"/"0" (any case); ValueError for anything else.
- `static fn tryParse(s: string) -> bool?` — As parse, but null for anything else.
- `static fn compare(a: bool, b: bool) -> int` — A comparator for sorting: false before true.
- `static fn descending(a: bool, b: bool) -> int`
- `static fn compareTo(a: bool, b: bool) -> int`
- `static fn toInt(b: bool) -> int` — 1 or 0.
- `static fn toString(b: bool) -> string` — "true" or "false".
- `static fn toYesNo(b: bool) -> string` — "yes" or "no".
- `static fn toOnOff(b: bool) -> string` — "on" or "off".
- `static fn xor(a: bool, b: bool) -> bool` — Whether exactly one of the two is true.
- `static fn implies(a: bool, b: bool) -> bool` — `a` implies `b`: false only when a is true and b is false.
